content.title: About
content.content: Whiskey is a distilled spirit made from fermented grain mash and aged in oak barrels. Major types include Scotch, Irish, American (bourbon) and Canadian whiskey. Flavors range from light and fruity to rich, smoky, and spicy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest recorded whiskey recipe dates back to 15th‑century Scotland.
The word “whiskey” comes from the Gaelic “uisge beatha,” meaning “water of life.”
Bourbon must be aged at least two years in new charred oak barrels.
Scotch whiskey is categorized into single malt and blended varieties.
In 2018, over 1.2 billion litres of Scotch whisky were sold worldwide.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols in aged whiskey may help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Moderate intake supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Studies suggest that small amounts (30–40 ml daily) can raise HDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: May lower risk of type 2 diabetes
items.content: Epidemiological data link moderate alcohol consumption with reduced diabetes risk.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Traditionally, whiskey is enjoyed as a digestif because it stimulates gastric secretions.

items.title: Social and cultural benefits
items.content: Responsible sharing can promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol dependence
items.content: Regular consumption can lead to addiction and adverse health effects.

items.title: Liver disease risk
items.content: Excessive intake is associated with cirrhosis and other liver conditions.

items.title: Impaired cognition and coordination
items.content: Alcohol reduces reaction time and can increase accident risk.

items.title: Interactions with medications
items.content: Whiskey may potentiate the effects of sedatives and anticoagulants.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: A 100 ml serving contains roughly 220 kcal, which should be considered in weight management.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Whiskey is typically served in small glasses (30–50 ml) at room temperature. It can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or in classic cocktails such as Old Fashioned, Manhattan, and Whiskey Sour. For tasting, a tulip‑shaped glass with a wide bowl is recommended.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place upright so the cork does not stay in contact with the liquid. After opening, it’s best consumed within 1–2 years, as prolonged exposure to air can alter the flavor.
